answer.rationale: The binding constraint is not cost alone but cost under zero delivery slack: 14 days to expiry, 94% of committed volume, no buffer. That rules out switch_primary_vendor this cycle even though memory_c2 is the single most attractive record against an 18% mandate — a migration inside 14 days with no buffer converts a price win into a line-stoppage risk, and c2's onboarding speed was observed in an unstated volume regime that may not have been a no-buffer one. defer_decision is unavailable in substance: c5 worked because the renewal was non-critical and could ride month-to-month; primary supply that does not auto-renew has no such fallback. add_second_source (c3) is the right structural answer to single-point-of-failure but is a build, not a 14-day move, and it adds qualification spend in a year where spend must fall 18%. That leaves negotiate_terms, which is the only direction that can move cost inside the window without touching the physical supply path: c4 shows benchmarking moved the incumbent on both price and terms, c1 shows the integration is stable so I am negotiating from a working baseline, and c6 shows volume commitment is a real lever. I verify c2 and c4 rather than the memories I am acting on most comfortably: c2 because it is the tempting counterfactual and I need to know whether its cost win came at comparable volume and criticality before I decline it, and c4 because it is load-bearing for my chosen action and I need the actual magnitude recovered and whether it was this component class or a smaller one. If c4's recovery was a few points on a minor line, negotiation alone will not reach 18% and the honest answer becomes a negotiated bridge plus second-sourcing next cycle. Downstream risk I am flagging explicitly: c6 invites a multi-year lock to capture volume pricing, and that is exactly the move that would foreclose both switching (c2) and second-sourcing (c3) in later cycles. I intend to negotiate price and payment terms against benchmark while keeping term length short enough to preserve those options, treating the volume-pricing tradeoff as unresolved rather than settled. The 18% target may not be fully reachable this cycle from negotiation alone; I would rather report a partial gain with the supply path intact than book the full cut and carry a migration through a no-buffer line.
